## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sobhitabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 8) is a biographical poem situated in the *Buddhavaṁsa* of the Pali Khuddakanikāya, chronicling the life, awakening, and dispensation of the past Buddha Sobhita [SuttaCentral]. Within the structural schema of the *Buddhavaṁsa*, each chapter normally presents the biography of a past Buddha alongside an embedded history of the Bodhisatta (the future Gotama Buddha) during that era, detailing his status and his *adhitthāna* ("determination") to fulfill the ten perfections (*pāramīs*) [Gaffney 2003]. Unusually, this formal resolution to fulfill the *pāramīs* is omitted in the *Sobhitabuddhavaṁsa* (a feature shared only with the *Koṇḍaññabuddhavaṁsa*), whereas the remaining Buddha chronicles include this programmatic dedication [Gaffney 2003].
According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits extensive internal text reuse across the Pali corpus, recording 388 matches with 29 texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most pervasive intertextual relationship is with the *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā* (139 matches), alongside high structural and formulaic alignment with adjacent chapters of the *Buddhavaṁsa*, particularly the *Sumedhabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 13), *Revatabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 7), *Sikhībuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 22), and *Padumuttarabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 12) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments align segments of the text with Tibetan versions of the *Jātakanidāna* (D0032) and the *Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśasūtra* (D0047), as well as sparse parallels in the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
